payment/medusa/orderItemQuantities#never.note: Suspected real bug at the module's action level. With positive quantities: fulfil 1, return 1, receive 1, return 1, receive 1 leaves return_received_quantity 2 for 1 fulfilled: RETURN_ITEM (return-item.ts:51-61) checks `fulfilled - return_requested` and forgets what was already received. The search's run is a negative quantity: CANCEL_RETURN_ITEM of -2 passes `!quantity` and `-2 > return_requested` and raises return_requested to 2 with nothing fulfilled. @medusajs/order@2.22.0 does both. The admin route that feeds RETURN_ITEM takes `quantity: z.number()` with no minimum (api/admin/returns/validators.ts:128) and request-item-return.ts:99-104 checks no quantity; whether something else upstream stops either was not found.

recheck.evidence: Partly fixed upstream: 879fb819 (#17431, 2026-10-23, released in 2.22.1) makes RETURN_ITEM subtract return_received_quantity and return_dismissed_quantity too (return-item.ts:51-58), so the positive run (fulfil 1, return, receive, return, receive) is refused on 2.22.1. The search's run is not: CANCEL_RETURN_ITEM of -2 (cancel-return.ts:44-56, unchanged) still raises return_requested to 2 with nothing fulfilled on 2.22.1, and the admin returns validators still take quantity z.number() with no minimum (validators.ts:128). The rule mirrors 2.22.0, where both happen.

payment/medusa/orderItemQuantities#never.note: Suspected real bug at the module's action level (lower confidence: the claim workflows that emit WRITE_OFF_ITEM were not traced). WRITE_OFF_ITEM (write-off-item.ts:48-53) compares one action's quantity with the item's quantity, not the total written off: two write-offs of 2 on an item of 2 write off 4. The search's run: REINSTATE_ITEM of -3 (any quantity not above the item's passes) raises written_off_quantity to 3 of 2. The original does both.

recheck.evidence: write-off-item.ts is unchanged (:41-49 compares one action's quantity with the item's); on 2.22.1 two write-offs of 2 still write off 4 of 2, and REINSTATE_ITEM of -3 still raises written_off to 3.

payment/vendure/orderProcess#a placed or.note: Suspected real bug. Local search: unknown (a state witness, no run within 3 s); a run exists and the original does it: Created, AddingItems, ArrangingPayment, PaymentAuthorized, ArrangingAdditionalPayment, Cancelled with a line still of quantity 1. default-order-process.ts:283-285 `if (toState === 'Cancelled') { return; }` inside the checkAdditionalPaymentsAmount block returns from onTransitionStart itself, so checkAllItemsBeforeCancel (:364-374, documented at :115-121 'Prevents transition to the Cancelled state unless all OrderItems are already cancelled. @default true') never runs from ArrangingAdditionalPayment; from PaymentAuthorized the same cancel is refused. Found by the conformance harness first (as a modelling error in the rule, fixed).

recheck.evidence: default-order-process.ts still returns from onTransitionStart on `toState === 'Cancelled'` inside the checkAdditionalPaymentsAmount block (:287-289), before checkAllItemsBeforeCancel (:416-425). The rule conforms to @vendure/core@3.8.1's OrderStateMachine on 3000 random runs, and on 3.8.1 PaymentAuthorized, ArrangingAdditionalPayment, Cancelled cancels an order with a live line (from PaymentAuthorized the same cancel is refused).

payment/vendure/orderProcess#an order sh.note: Not refuted by the local search (unknown), but a run breaks it and Vendure 2.2.7 does it: Created, AddingItems, ArrangingPayment, PaymentAuthorized, Modifying, Shipped with only an Authorized payment (createFulfillment checks no payment state, and ArrangingAdditionalPayment counts Authorized payments as covering). An inferred law that overstated the intent: restated as 'an order ships only once its payment is authorized or settled'.
The restatement of 'an order ships only once its payment has settled' (see that entry).

payment/solidus/Payment#refunds never ex.note: Suspected real bug (from the source; ActiveRecord models, not run). With the default configuration a Spree::Refund of the whole amount is valid on a pending (authorized) payment (refund.rb:89-109; refundable_payment_states default %w[completed pending]), and a later partial capture! sets the payment's amount to what was captured (processing.rb:88 `update!(amount: captured_amount)`), below the refunds: credit_allowed (payment.rb:93-95) goes negative. The search's run takes the deprecated path (a refund while processing, allowed unless require_refundable_payment_state), then pend, then capture! of 2 of 6.
